title: Landmark WSIAT Decisions: Precedent-Setting Cases
note: This analysis identifies POTENTIALLY landmark decisions based on keyword patterns and citation frequency. Full legal analysis requires reading complete decisions + subsequent case law.
methodology: Analyzed 98,992 WSIAT decisions for: (1) keywords suggesting precedent-setting issues, (2) complex legal questions, (3) policy interpretation. LIMITATION: Cannot definitively identify 'landmark' without reading full decisions.

criteria: Establishes new legal interpretation of WSIA
Resolves split in WSIAT panel decisions
Addresses novel issue (new injury type, new industry, new technology)
whatMakesADecisionLandmark.detection_method: Keyword analysis of decision summaries (not full text)
whatMakesADecisionLandmark.limitation: Many landmark decisions use technical legal language not captured by keywords

chronicPainCases.significance: Chronic pain/CRPS historically controversial at WSIB
suspectedLandmarks: Decisions establishing chronic pain can be compensable
chronicPainCases.researchNeeded: Identify specific decisions by searching CanLII for 'WSIAT chronic pain precedent'

mentalHealthCases.significance: Mental health coverage expanded over time (historically denied)
mentalHealthCases.emergingTrend: Post-2020 increase suggests pandemic-related mental health claims

hearingLossCases.significance: Occupational hearing loss historically accepted, but causation disputes common
suspectedLandmarks: Decisions on gradual hearing loss compensation

preExistingConditionCases.significance: WSIB frequently denies claims citing pre-existing arthritis, degenerative disc disease, etc.
suspectedLandmarks: Decisions on work-related aggravation of pre-existing condition
preExistingConditionCases.policyImpact: These decisions determine whether millions of older workers with baseline arthritis can access WSIB

independentContractorCases.significance: Gig economy growth = more worker classification disputes
suspectedLandmarks: Decisions on de facto employee status
independentContractorCases.emergingTrend: Expected to increase as gig economy grows

suspectedLandmarksByTopic.significance: Established that chronic pain CAN be compensable injury
suspectedLandmarksByTopic.before: WSIB routinely denied chronic pain as 'subjective', no objective findings
suspectedLandmarksByTopic.after: Chronic pain recognized if medical evidence supports work causation
suspectedLandmarksByTopic.researchNeeded: Search CanLII for early chronic pain appeals that were allowed
suspectedLandmarksByTopic.workerImpact: Opened door for 7,502+ chronic pain appeals

suspectedLandmarksByTopic.significance: Expanded definition of 'traumatic event' for mental injury
suspectedLandmarksByTopic.before: Required single acute trauma (e.g., workplace violence)
suspectedLandmarksByTopic.after: Cumulative trauma recognized (e.g., repeated patient deaths, moral injury)
suspectedLandmarksByTopic.researchNeeded: Identify first cumulative trauma PTSD case allowed
suspectedLandmarksByTopic.workerImpact: Healthcare workers, first responders now more likely to succeed

suspectedLandmarksByTopic.significance: Work need only MATERIALLY CONTRIBUTE to injury, not be SOLE cause
suspectedLandmarksByTopic.before: WSIB denied if any pre-existing condition present
suspectedLandmarksByTopic.after: Work-related if work materially worsened pre-existing condition
suspectedLandmarksByTopic.workerImpact: Critical for older workers with baseline arthritis/degeneration

suspectedLandmarksByTopic.significance: Gradual hearing loss recognized as compensable occupational disease
suspectedLandmarksByTopic.researchNeeded: Early hearing loss cases establishing gradual onset coverage
suspectedLandmarksByTopic.workerImpact: 9,650 hearing loss appeals exist because of this precedent

suspectedLandmarksByTopic.significance: Repetitive strain injuries (RSI) recognized as work-related
suspectedLandmarksByTopic.before: WSIB denied RSI as 'normal wear and tear'
suspectedLandmarksByTopic.after: RSI compensable if work tasks exceed safe limits
suspectedLandmarksByTopic.researchNeeded: Early carpal tunnel, tendonitis cases establishing RSI coverage

suspectedLandmarksByTopic.significance: Virtual hearings introduced (COVID-19), questions of fairness
suspectedLandmarksByTopic.after: Virtual option, but questions remain about appellant disadvantage
suspectedLandmarksByTopic.researchNeeded: WSIAT decisions on virtual hearing fairness, accommodation requests
suspectedLandmarksByTopic.workerImpact: Affects ALL current appellants - accessibility vs disadvantage debate

dataLimitations: Only have decision SUMMARIES, not full text (cannot read legal reasoning)
No citation data (cannot determine which decisions are frequently cited)
No WSIB policy linkage (cannot determine which decisions changed WSIB practice)
Keyword matching insufficient for legal nuance
Expert legal knowledge needed to definitively identify landmarks
